questions.def: 'Had begun' indicates the movie started before his arrival.
questions.question: By the time he arrived, the movie ___ already begun.

questions.def: 'Had lost' shows the action happened before realizing.
questions.question: She ___ her keys when she realized she had left the oven on.

questions.def: 'Had lived' refers to a past action before another past action.
questions.question: They ___ in Paris before moving to Rome.

questions.def: 'Had paid' expresses regret about a past action.
questions.question: I wish I ___ more attention in class yesterday.

questions.def: Expresses regret about a past action, uses past perfect.
questions.question: If only I ___ harder when I was a student.

questions.def: Past perfect to show completion before another past action.
questions.question: By the time we got there, they ___ the project.

questions.def: 'Knew' expresses a hypothetical or untrue situation.
questions.question: He acted as if he ___ the answer.

questions.def: Past perfect shows completion before a past event.
questions.question: He ___ his report before the deadline arrived.

questions.def: Third conditional requires past perfect in the 'if' clause.
questions.question: If he ___ harder, he would have passed the exam.

questions.def: 'Was raining' describes a continuous past action.
questions.question: It ___ raining when I left the house.

questions.def: Past perfect indicates a completed action before another past action.
questions.question: Before she became a writer, she ___ as a teacher.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous for an action continuing until a past time.
questions.question: They ___ for hours before the train arrived.

questions.def: 'Would' is the past form of 'will' in reported speech.
questions.question: She said she ___ call me later.

questions.def: 'Went' expresses a completed action in the past.
questions.question: I ___ to see him yesterday, but he wasn't home.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had been' sets context relative to a past event.
questions.question: It ___ a long time since we last met.

questions.def: 'Should have' indicates expectation or obligation in the past.
questions.question: He ___ have finished the report by now.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had escaped' before police arrival (simple past).
questions.question: By the time the police arrived, the thief ___.

questions.def: Should be 'had already left', not 'has already left'.
questions.question: She has already left before I arrived.

questions.def: 'Had known' expresses regret about a past lack of knowledge.
questions.question: I wish I ___ the answer then.

questions.def: Third conditional: 'would have' + past participle.
questions.question: He ___ to the concert if he had bought tickets.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous: ongoing action before stopping.
questions.question: She ___ the piano for years before stopping.

questions.def: 'Last year' requires simple past: 'visited', not 'have visited'.
questions.question: They have visited Paris last year.

questions.def: Past perfect needed: 'had eaten', to indicate sequence.
questions.question: He said he ___ already ___ before we arrived.

questions.def: 'I'd rather' + past simple for preferences.
questions.question: I'd rather you ___ smoke in here.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous: action leading to a past result.
questions.question: The rain ___ all morning, so the ground was wet.

questions.def: Past perfect continuous shows duration of an action before another past action.
questions.question: By the time the ambulance arrived, he ___ for almost an hour.

questions.def: 'Seem to have + past participle' expresses a past action with present relevance.
questions.question: I ___ my keys; I can't remember where I last saw them.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had lived' indicates an action completed before another past action.
questions.question: He ___ in Paris before moving to Rome.

questions.def: 'Was going to' expresses an unfulfilled intention in the past.
questions.question: I ___ to call you yesterday, but I forgot.

questions.def: 'Might have' expresses a possibility that was not realised.
questions.question: She ___ been happier, but she kept her feelings private.
